'''Steven Victor Ley''' (born 10 December 1945) is Professor of Organic Chemistry in the [[Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge|Department of Chemistry]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], and is a Fellow of [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].  He was President of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (2000–2002) and was made a [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] in January 2002, in the process. In 2011, he was included by ''The Times'' in the list of the "100 most important people in British science".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rsc.org/AboutUs/News/PressReleases/2010/EurekaScience100.asp |title = Chemistry makes its mark on science top 100}}</ref><ref>[http://www.beilstein.tv/tvpost/introducing-the-innovative-technology-centre/ Video with Steven Ley:] "Introducing the Innovative Technology Centre"</ref><ref name="LeyThomas2003">{{cite journal|last1=Ley|first1=Steven V.|last2=Thomas|first2=Andrew W.|title=Modern Synthetic Methods for Copper-Mediated C(aryl)—O, C(aryl)—N, and C(aryl)—S Bond Formation|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=42|issue=44|year=2003|pages=5400–5449|issn=1433-7851|doi=10.1002/anie.200300594|pmid=14618572}}</ref><ref name=homepage>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150927063810/http://www.leygroup.ch.cam.ac.uk/|archive-date=27 September 2015|url=http://www.leygroup.ch.cam.ac.uk/|title=Professor Steven V. Ley CBE FRS Organic Chemistry Research Group|publisher=[[University of Cambridge]]}}</ref>

==Education==
Ley was educated at [[Stamford School|Stamford]] and [[Loughborough University|Loughborough University of Technology]] where he was awarded a Bachelor of Science and PhD.<ref name=leyswhoA/><ref name=leyphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Loughborough|title=Studies in the chemistry of benzobicyclo systems.|first= Steven Victor|last=Ley|year=1972|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.463214|oclc=801311581}}</ref>

==Research==
Ley's main research field are the [[total synthesis]] of [[biomolecule]]s. His group has published extensively on this topic, and has completed the synthesis of more than 140 natural target compounds, with notable examples including indanamycin, routiennocin, avermectin B1a, okadaic acid, spongistatin, [[thapsigargin]], [[epothilone|epothilone A]], antascomicin B, bengazole A and [[rapamycin]]. His total synthesis of [[azadirachtin]], completed in 2007, is widely regarded as one of the major landmarks in total synthesis. In the course of this work, he has also made substantial advances in many areas of organic chemistry, including the development of new [[catalyst]]s, [[protecting group]]s and [[reagent]]s.  He is one of the inventors of [[Tetrapropylammonium perruthenate|TPAP]], a widely employed oxidising reagent. He has also pioneered the use of immobilised reagents and flow techniques in multi-step organic synthesis. This work now incorporates [[flow chemistry]] for multistep organic synthesis applications.

By 2020, Ley had published 888 academic research papers spanning his career of 50 years.<ref>{{cite magazine |magazine=Chemistry at Cambridge Magazine |issue=61 |page=9 |url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/files/chematcam/Winter2020ChemCampdf1.8mb.pdf#page=9 |title=50 years and 888 papers |date=2020 |access-date=2023-02-12}}</ref>
